action_change_recommendation: Same as Claude. Structurally there is no 'sibling' measurability lemma in Mathlib that closes Measurable (pdf ...) without going through Measure.measurable_rnDeriv, because pdf is defined as rnDeriv. The carve-out for sibling-lemma closures doesn't help here.
contract_question: On canonical OPEN row current_scale_0163 (measurable_pdf), does ANY of 8 hand-curated candidate tactics (fun_prop, measurability, simp/exact variants on sibling measurability lemmas, NOT measurable_rnDeriv) produce a literal Lean-verified closure? rationale_short: Definitional: pdf X ℙ μ ≡ (map X ℙ).rnDeriv μ by pdf_def : ... := rfl. So Measurable (pdf X ℙ μ) reduces by rfl to Measurable ((map X ℙ).rnDeriv μ), and the ONLY direct lemma is measurable_rnDeriv (which is @[fun_prop]). Any non-leaky closure requires either a new analytic fact (rnDeriv-of-map-is-measurable via a different route) or unfolding through Lebesgue decomposition. Both are out of scope for type-aware top-k smoke test.
